annotation.kind: source-faithful componentwise realization of the XX-star-X forward-error term in equation (6.6)

assumptions: The task is the real square-matrix specialization of the paper's complex-matrix calculation, so conjugate transpose becomes transpose.
The two matrix products in XX-transpose-X are computed entry by entry with sequential rounded dot products under the standard relative-error model, excluding overflow and underflow.
The displayed majorant keeps the two local matrix-product errors explicit instead of suppressing their dimension-dependent coefficient in the paper's epsilon notation.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P28 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P28 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p28_t1_newton_schulz_triple_product_error (fp : P28FPModel) (n : Nat) (X : P28RealMatrix n) (hvalid : P28GammaValid fp.u n) : forall i j, abs (p28RoundedGramTriple fp X i j - p28ExactGramTriple X i j) <= p28GramTripleErrorMajorant fp X i j
formal_statement.plain_language: The entrywise forward error from computing XX-transpose-X with two rounded matrix products is bounded by the sum of the second product's local error majorant and the first product's error propagated through the final multiplication.

informal_proof: Split the final difference into the local error of multiplying the computed Gram matrix by X and the first Gram-product error propagated through multiplication by X. Apply the componentwise rounded matrix-product bound to each of the two products and use the triangle inequality.
informal_statement: The forward-error term epsilon_1 in equation (6.6), made explicit for the paper's prescribed two-product evaluation of XX-star-X.
